question.text: Consider the system of linear equations \[ \left\{ \begin{align*} &2x_1+2x_2 +4x_3= -4\\ &x_2+2x_3 =-6. \end{align*} \right. \] Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.explanation:
The augmented matrix for this system is \[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 2 & 2 & 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6 \\ \end{array} \right]. \]

Using the standard Gauss-Jordan method, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

\[\begin{align*} M&=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 2 & 2 & 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_1&:=\dfrac12R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_1 &:=R_1+(-1)R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -6 \\ \end{array}\right] \end{align*}\]

The corresponding system is now

\[ \left\{ \begin{align*} &x_1 =4\\ &x_2+2x_3=-6. \end{align*} \right. \] The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x_1$ and $x_2,$ and we have one free variable, $x_3.$ Since we have that $x_1= 4$, we only need to find $x_2$ in terms of $x_3.$

Therefore, the general solution is

\[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x_1=4 \\ x_2=-6-2x_3, \end{array} \right. \]

where $x_3$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

\begin{align*} \begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ -6-2x_3 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad x_3 \in (-\infty,\infty). \end{align*}

example.title: Solving a Consistent System of Equations Using Gauss-Jordan Elimination

question.text:
Consider the following system of equations. \[ \left\{ \begin{align*} &3x +2y= -3\\ &-6x-4y =6, \end{align*} \right. \] which of the following statements are true?

  1. The system is consistent independent
  2. The system is consistent dependent
  3. The system has no solution
question.explanation:
To classify the system, we first need to find the solution to the system. The augmented matrix for this system is \[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 3 & 2 & -3 \\ -6 & -4 & 6 \end{array} \right]. \]

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to reduced row echelon form as follows:

\[\begin{align*} M&= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 3 & 2 & -3 \\ -6 & -4 & 6 \end{array}\right]& R_2 &:= R_2 + 2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 3 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}\]

The system is now
\[ \left\{ \begin{align*} &3x +2y= -3\\ &0x+0y =0. \end{align*} \right. \]

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

\[ 3x +2y= -3 \]

The basic variable is $x,$ and we have a free variable $y.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y.$

Therefore, since there are infinitely many solutions, we conclude that the system is consistent dependent.

As a result, only statement II is true.

question.text:
Determine the value of $k$ for which the following system of linear equations is consistent dependent:

\[ \left\{ \begin{align*} &2x -2y =4\\ &-3x+ky =- 6 \end{align*} \right. \]
question.explanation:
The augmented matrix for this system is

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & -2 & 4 \\ -3 & k & -6 \\ \end{array} \right]. \]

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form, as follows:

\[\begin{align*} M&= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & -2 & 4 \\ -3 & k & -6 \\ \end{array}\right]& R_2 &:= R_2+ \dfrac32 R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & k-3 & 0 \\ \end{array}\right] \end{align*}\]

The corresponding system is now

\[ \left\{ \begin{align*} & 2x -2y = 4 \\ & \left(k-3\right)y = 0. \end{align*} \right. \]

The system is consistent dependent if it has infinitely many solutions. For the system to have infinitely many solutions, it must have at least one free variable.

If $k=3,$ then the second equation is $0=0,$ which is true for any value of $y$,. So, we can remove this equation from the system. As a result, the system will contain only one equation, $2x + 2y = 4.$

Then, the basic variable will be $x,$ and we will have a free variable $y.$ That means the system will have infinitely many solutions.

Therefore, our system is consistent dependent when $k=3.$

question.text:
Consider the following system of equations \[ \left\{ \begin{align*} &x + 2y =-1 \\ &3x + 7y= 1 \\ &-2x - 4y = 2. \end{align*} \right. \] Which of the following statements are true?

  1. The system is consistent independent
  2. The system has no solution
  3. The system is consistent dependent
question.explanation:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is \[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & 7 & 1 \\ -2 & -4 & 2 \end{array} \right]. \] Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

\[\begin{align*} M&= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 3 & 7 & 1 \\ -2 & -4 & 2 \end{array}\right]& R_2 &:= R_2+(-3)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ -2 & -4 & 2 \end{array}\right]& R_3 &:= R_3+2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}\]

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ are solutions to the third equation $0x+0y=0$, we can remove this equation from the system. So, the corresponding system is now

\[ \begin{cases} x +2y =-1\\ y = 4. \end{cases} \]

From the second equation we have $y=4$ and substituting this into the first equation yields $x=-9.$ So, we conclude that the system is consistent independent.

As a result, only statement I is true.

question.text:
Consider the following system of equations. \[ \left\{ \begin{align*} &x - y + z = 3 \\ &-3x + 3y - 3z = 10 \end{align*} \right. \] Which of the following statements are true?

  1. The system is inconsistent
  2. The system has a unique solution
  3. The system is consistent dependent
question.explanation:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & -3 & 10 \end{array} \right]. \]

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

\[\begin{align*} M&= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & -3 & 10 \end{array}\right]& R_2 &:= R_2+3R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 19 \end{array}\right] \end{align*}\]

The final row corresponds to the equation $0x+0y+0z=19,$ and this has no solution. Therefore, our system has no solution, and we conclude that the system is inconsistent.

As a result, only statement I is true.
